questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The main function of cadmium used in the nuclear reactor is:
options: To capture the slow neutron produced in the nuclear reactor
It slows down the fast moving secondary neutrons produced during the nuclear fission
It gives energy to the secondary neutrons produced in the nuclear fission
It removes the heat produced at the core of the reactor
questions.solution:
In a nuclear reactor, cadmium rods are used as control rods.

The primary function of control rods is to absorb or capture the slow neutrons produced during the nuclear fission reaction, thereby controlling the rate of the chain reaction.

Moderators (like heavy water or graphite) are used to slow down fast-moving neutrons, while coolants (like water or liquid sodium) are used to remove the heat produced at the core.

Answer: To capture the slow neutron produced in the nuclear reactor

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The atomic mass of an element ${}_{10}X^{20}$ is 19.98170 amu. The binding energy per nucleon of that element is:
[given mass of neutron = 1.00867 amu and mass of proton = 1.00783 amu and 1amu = 931 MeV]
questions.solution:
Number of protons, $Z = 10$

Number of neutrons, $A - Z = 20 - 10 = 10$

Total mass of nucleons $= 10 m_p + 10 m_n$

Total mass of nucleons $= 10(1.00783) + 10(1.00867) = 10.0783 + 10.0867 = 20.1650$ amu

Mass defect, $\Delta m = \text{Mass of nucleons} - \text{Mass of nucleus}$

$\Delta m = 20.1650 - 19.98170 = 0.1833$ amu

Total binding energy, $BE = \Delta m \times 931$ MeV

$BE = 0.1833 \times 931 = 170.6523$ MeV

Binding energy per nucleon $= \dfrac{BE}{A} = \dfrac{170.6523}{20} = 8.5326$ MeV/nucleon $\approx 8.533$ MeV/nucleon

Answer: $8.533$ MeV / nucleon

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the ratio of the nuclear radii of two atoms is 2:3 then the ratio of their mass numbers is:
questions.solution:
The nuclear radius $R$ is related to the mass number $A$ by the empirical formula:

$R = R_0 A^{1/3}$

where $R_0$ is a constant.

The ratio of the nuclear radii of two atoms is given by:

$\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \left(\dfrac{A_1}{A_2}\right)^{1/3}$

Given $\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \dfrac{2}{3}$, substituting this value:

$\dfrac{2}{3} = \left(\dfrac{A_1}{A_2}\right)^{1/3}$

Cubing both sides:

$\dfrac{A_1}{A_2} = \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^3 = \dfrac{8}{27}$

The ratio of their mass numbers is $8:27$.

Answer: $8:27$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two deuterons are fused to form one alpha particle. If binding energy per nucleon of deuterium is 1.05 MeV and that of alpha particle is 7 MeV, what is the energy released in the formation of one alpha particle from the fusing of two deuterons?
questions.solution:
The fusion reaction is given by:

$2\ ^{2}_{1}\text{H} \rightarrow\ ^{4}_{2}\text{He}$

Total binding energy of two deuterons = $2 \times (2 \times 1.05) = 4.2\ \text{MeV}$

Total binding energy of one alpha particle = $4 \times 7 = 28\ \text{MeV}$

Energy released = Total binding energy of products - Total binding energy of reactants

Energy released = $28 - 4.2 = 23.8\ \text{MeV}$

Answer: $23.8\ \text{MeV}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A nucleus of uranium-235 absorbs a slow neutron and undergoes nuclear fission according to the reaction: ${}^{235}_{92}U + {}^{1}_{0}n \rightarrow {}^{141}_{56}Ba + {}^{92}_{36}Kr + 3{}^{1}_{0}n + Q$
If the average energy released per fission is 202 MeV, the energy released when 2.35 g of $U^{235}$ undergoes complete fission is approximately;
[Given $1eV = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\ J$, Avogadro number $= 6.02 \times 10^{23}$]
questions.solution:
Number of moles of $U^{235} = \dfrac{2.35}{235} = 0.01$ mol

Number of atoms of $U^{235} = 0.01 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} = 6.02 \times 10^{21}$

Energy released per fission $= 202 \text{ MeV} = 202 \times 10^6 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J} = 3.232 \times 10^{-11}\text{ J}$

Total energy released $= 6.02 \times 10^{21} \times 3.232 \times 10^{-11}\text{ J}$

Total energy released $= 19.456 \times 10^{10}\text{ J}$

Answer: $19.45 \times 10^{10}\ J$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A mercury-198 nucleus is bombarded by a neutron, which causes a nuclear reaction
${}^{1}_{0}n + {}^{198}_{80}Hg \longrightarrow {}^{197}_{79}Au + X$
What is the unknown product particle X?
questions.solution:
Let the unknown particle $X$ be represented as ${}^{A}_{Z}X$.

Applying the principle of conservation of mass number:
$1 + 198 = 197 + A$
$199 = 197 + A$
$A = 2$

Applying the principle of conservation of atomic number:
$0 + 80 = 79 + Z$
$80 = 79 + Z$
$Z = 1$

The particle with mass number $A = 2$ and atomic number $Z = 1$ is ${}^{2}_{1}H$, which is a deuteron.

Answer: Deuteron

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a nitrogen-14 nucleus is bombarded by a deuteron, the products formed are:
options: Nitrogen-15 nucleus and an alpha particle
Nitrogen-15 nucleus and a beta particle
Carbon-12 nucleus and an alpha particle
Carbon- 12 nucleus and a beta particle
questions.solution:
The nuclear reaction: $^{14}_7N + ^2_1H \to ^A_ZX + ^4_2He$

Conservation of mass number: $14 + 2 = A + 4 \Rightarrow A = 12$

Conservation of atomic number: $7 + 1 = Z + 2 \Rightarrow Z = 6$

$Z = 6$ corresponds to Carbon, $A = 12$ gives Carbon-12.

$^{14}_7N + ^2_1H \to ^{12}_6C + ^4_2He$

The products are Carbon-12 nucleus and an alpha particle.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a deuterium-tritium fusion reaction given by ${ }_1^2 \mathrm{H}+{ }_1^3 \mathrm{H} \rightarrow{ }_2^4 \mathrm{He}+{ }_0^1 n$ the mass defect is given as 0.0188 u . The total energy released in the fusion reaction is:
questions.solution:
The energy released in a nuclear reaction is calculated using the mass defect $\Delta m$ and the conversion factor $1 \text{ u} = 931.5 \text{ MeV}/c^2$.

Given the mass defect $\Delta m = 0.0188 \text{ u}$.

The energy released $Q$ is given by $Q = \Delta m \times 931.5 \text{ MeV}/\text{u}$.

$Q = 0.0188 \times 931.5 \text{ MeV}$.

$Q \approx 17.5122 \text{ MeV}$.

Rounding to the nearest provided option, the energy released is $17.5 \text{ MeV}$.

Answer: 17.5 MeV

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a nuclear reaction ${ }_4^{10} \mathrm{Be}+{ }_1^1 p \rightarrow{ }_5^{10} \mathrm{~B}+{ }_0^1 n$, what is the total energy released if the binding energy of beryllium -9 is 58.2 MeV and that of boron- 10 is 64.7 MeV ?
questions.solution:
The nuclear reaction is given by ${}_{4}^{10}\text{Be} + {}_{1}^{1}\text{p} \rightarrow {}_{5}^{10}\text{B} + {}_{0}^{1}\text{n}$.

The energy released in a nuclear reaction is given by the difference in the total binding energy of the products and the reactants. $Q = \text{BE}(\text{products}) - \text{BE}(\text{reactants})$.

The binding energy of ${}_{1}^{1}\text{p}$ (proton) is $0$ MeV and the binding energy of ${}_{0}^{1}\text{n}$ (neutron) is $0$ MeV.

The binding energy of ${}_{4}^{10}\text{Be}$ is given as $58.2$ MeV and the binding energy of ${}_{5}^{10}\text{B}$ is $64.7$ MeV.

$Q = [\text{BE}({}_{5}^{10}\text{B}) + \text{BE}({}_{0}^{1}\text{n})] - [\text{BE}({}_{4}^{10}\text{Be}) + \text{BE}({}_{1}^{1}\text{p})]$

$Q = [64.7 + 0] - [58.2 + 0] = 6.5 \text{ MeV}$.

To convert the energy from MeV to Joules, we use the conversion factor $1 \text{ eV} = 1.602 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J}$.

$Q = 6.5 \times 10^{6} \times 1.602 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J} \approx 10.413 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J} = 1.0413 \times 10^{-12} \text{ J}$.

Rounding to the nearest value provided in the options, we get $1.04 \times 10^{-12} \text{ J}$.

Answer: $1.04 \times 10^{-12} J$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Fusion reaction is more energetic than fission reaction because
options: In the fusion reaction lighter nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus
Uncontrolled chain reaction is taking place In the fusion reaction.
The energy released per unit mass of the fuel in fusion reaction is larger than the energy released per unit mass of the fuel in fission reaction.
Fusion reaction is taking place at very high temperature
questions.solution:
The energy released in a nuclear reaction is determined by the mass defect, which is the difference between the mass of the reactants and the mass of the products. This mass defect is converted into energy according to Einstein's mass-energy equivalence relation, $E = \Delta m c^2$.

In fission, a heavy nucleus splits into two lighter nuclei, whereas in fusion, two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus. The binding energy per nucleon curve shows that the binding energy per nucleon increases significantly when light nuclei fuse to form a medium-mass nucleus, compared to the change when a heavy nucleus undergoes fission.

Consequently, the energy released per unit mass of the fuel (the mass defect per unit mass of the reactants) is significantly higher for fusion reactions than for fission reactions. This makes fusion reactions more energetic per unit mass of the fuel involved.

Answer: The energy released per unit mass of the fuel in fusion reaction is larger than the energy released per unit mass of the fuel in fission reaction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The nucleus of oxygen atom contains 8 protons and 8 neutrons. What is the mass defect in amu?
[Given Mass of proton $=1.00727$ amu Mass of neutron $=1.00866 \mathrm{amu}$ and the mass of oxygen nucleus $=15.99053 \mathrm{amu}$.]
questions.solution:
The mass defect $\Delta m$ of a nucleus is defined as the difference between the sum of the masses of individual nucleons and the actual mass of the nucleus.

The formula for mass defect is given by:
$\Delta m = [Z \times m_p + (A - Z) \times m_n] - M_{nucleus}$

Given:
Number of protons $Z = 8$
Number of neutrons $N = A - Z = 16 - 8 = 8$
Mass of proton $m_p = 1.00727$ amu
Mass of neutron $m_n = 1.00866$ amu
Mass of oxygen nucleus $M_{nucleus} = 15.99053$ amu

Substituting the values:
$\Delta m = [8 \times 1.00727 + 8 \times 1.00866] - 15.99053$
$\Delta m = [8.05816 + 8.06928] - 15.99053$
$\Delta m = 16.12744 - 15.99053$
$\Delta m = 0.13691$ amu

Answer: 0.13691 amu

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: To get 300 MW electric power for half an hour, how much mass is to be completely converted into energy?
questions.solution:
The total energy $E$ required is given by the product of power $P$ and time $t$.

$P = 300 \text{ MW} = 300 \times 10^{6} \text{ W}$

$t = 30 \text{ minutes} = 30 \times 60 \text{ seconds} = 1800 \text{ s}$

$E = P \times t = 300 \times 10^{6} \times 1800 = 540000 \times 10^{6} = 5.4 \times 10^{11} \text{ J}$

Using Einstein mass-energy equivalence relation $E = mc^{2}$, where $c = 3 \times 10^{8} \text{ m/s}$ is the speed of light:

$m = \dfrac{E}{c^{2}} = \dfrac{5.4 \times 10^{11}}{(3 \times 10^{8})^{2}}$

$m = \dfrac{5.4 \times 10^{11}}{9 \times 10^{16}}$

$m = 0.6 \times 10^{-5} \text{ kg} = 6 \times 10^{-6} \text{ kg}$

Answer: $6 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~kg}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When ${ }^{10} \mathrm{~B}_5$ nuclei are bombarded by neutrons, one of the resultant nuclei is ${ }^7 \mathrm{Li}_3$. Then the emitted particle will be:
questions.solution:
The nuclear reaction can be represented as follows:

${}^{10}_{5}\text{B} + {}^{1}_{0}\text{n} \rightarrow {}^{7}_{3}\text{Li} + {}^{A}_{Z}\text{X}$

Applying the law of conservation of mass number (A):

$10 + 1 = 7 + A \Rightarrow 11 = 7 + A \Rightarrow A = 4$

Applying the law of conservation of atomic number (Z):

$5 + 0 = 3 + Z \Rightarrow 5 = 3 + Z \Rightarrow Z = 2$

The particle with mass number 4 and atomic number 2 is the alpha particle (${}^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ or $\alpha$).

Answer: Alpha particle

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Radium having mass number 200 and binding energy per nucleon 5.6 MeV , splits into two fragments Cadmium of mass number 112 and Hassium of mass number 108. If the binding energy per nucleon for Cadmium and Hassium is approximately 8.0 MeV , then the energy Q released per fission will be:
questions.solution:
The total binding energy of the parent nucleus (Radium) is given by the product of its mass number and its binding energy per nucleon.

Total binding energy of Radium = $200 \times 5.6 \text{ MeV} = 1120 \text{ MeV}$.

The total binding energy of the daughter nuclei (Cadmium and Hassium) is the sum of their individual binding energies.

Total binding energy of fragments = $(112 \times 8.0 \text{ MeV}) + (108 \times 8.0 \text{ MeV}) = (112 + 108) \times 8.0 \text{ MeV} = 220 \times 8.0 \text{ MeV} = 1760 \text{ MeV}$.

The energy released $Q$ in the fission process is the difference between the total binding energy of the products and the total binding energy of the reactant.

$Q = 1760 \text{ MeV} - 1120 \text{ MeV} = 640 \text{ MeV}$.

Answer: 640 MeV

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the mass numbers of two nuclei are in the ratio \(5: 2\) and their diameters are in ratio \(2: 6\), Then their nuclear densities will be in the ratio
questions.solution:
The nuclear radius $R$ is related to the mass number $A$ by the formula $R = R_{0} A^{1/3}$, where $R_{0}$ is a constant. The diameter $D$ is proportional to the radius, so $D \propto A^{1/3}$.

The nuclear density $\rho$ is defined as the ratio of the mass of the nucleus to its volume. The mass of a nucleus is approximately $M = A \times m_{p}$, where $m_{p}$ is the mass of a nucleon. The volume of a nucleus is $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi (R_{0} A^{1/3})^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_{0}^{3} A$.

The nuclear density is $\rho = \dfrac{M}{V} = \dfrac{A m_{p}}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_{0}^{3} A} = \dfrac{m_{p}}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_{0}^{3}}$.

Since $m_{p}$, $R_{0}$, and $\pi$ are constants, the nuclear density $\rho$ is independent of the mass number $A$. Therefore, the ratio of the nuclear densities of any two nuclei is always $1: 1$.

Answer: \(1: 1\)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Select the correct statement from the following:
options: Nuclear force is the weakest force in nature
Nuclear force is a non central force
Nuclear force depends on the charge of the nucleons
Nuclear force is a long range force
questions.solution:
Nuclear forces are the strongest forces in nature, acting between nucleons within the nucleus. They are short-range forces, effective only up to distances of the order of $10^{-15}$ m (femtometers).

Nuclear forces are charge-independent, meaning they act equally between proton-proton, neutron-neutron, and proton-neutron pairs, provided the distance is the same.

Nuclear forces are non-central forces, as they do not act only along the line joining the centers of the two nucleons; they depend on the spin and orientation of the nucleons.

Answer: Nuclear force is a non central force

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the binding energy per nucleon in ${ }_3 \mathrm{Li}^7$ and ${ }_2 \mathrm{He}^4$ nuclei are respectively 5.60 MeV and 7.06 MeV, then energy of p in the reaction $p+{ }_3 L i^7 \rightarrow 2{ }_2 H e^4$ is
questions.solution:
The given nuclear reaction is $p + _{3}Li^{7} \rightarrow 2_{2}He^{4}$.

The total binding energy of the reactants is:
Binding energy of $p$ = 0 MeV (since it is a single nucleon).
Binding energy of _{3}Li^{7} = 7 \times 5.60 \text{ MeV} = 39.20 \text{ MeV}$. \\ Total binding energy of reactants = $0 + 39.20 = 39.20 \text{ MeV}$. \\ \\ The total binding energy of the products is: \\ Binding energy of $2_{2}He^{4} = 2 \times (4 \times 7.06 \text{ MeV}) = 2 \times 28.24 \text{ MeV} = 56.48 \text{ MeV}$. \\ \\ The energy released ($Q$-value) in the reaction is the difference between the total binding energy of the products and the total binding energy of the reactants: \\ $Q = (\text{Total BE of products}) - (\text{Total BE of reactants})$ \\ $Q = 56.48 \text{ MeV} - 39.20 \text{ MeV} = 17.28 \text{ MeV}$.

Answer: 17.28 MeV$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a nuclear fusion reaction, two nuclei, $A$ and $B$ fuse to produce a nucleus $C$, releasing an amount of energy $\Delta \mathrm{E}$ in the process. If the mass defects of the three nuclei are $\Delta M_A, \Delta M_B$ and $\Delta M_C$ respectively, then which of the following relations is true? ( $c$ is the speed of light).
questions.solution:
Energy released in fusion: $\Delta E = BE_C - (BE_A + BE_B)$

Since $BE = \Delta M \cdot c^2$:

$\Delta E = (\Delta M_C)c^2 - [(\Delta M_A)c^2 + (\Delta M_B)c^2]$

Dividing by $c^2$:

$\dfrac{\Delta E}{c^2} = \Delta M_C - \Delta M_A - \Delta M_B$

$\Delta M_A + \Delta M_B = \Delta M_C - \dfrac{\Delta E}{c^2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The nuclear forces
a. are central forces, independent of the spin of the nucleons.
b. have a short-range dominant over a distance of about a few fermi
c. are stronger being hundred times stronger than that of electromagnetic forces.
d. are independent of the nuclear charge.

Which of the above is not true?
questions.solution:
Nuclear forces are known to be non-central forces, meaning they depend on the orientation of the spins of the nucleons. Therefore, the statement that they are central forces is incorrect.

Nuclear forces have a very short range, typically effective only within a few femtometers (fermi), which makes statement b true.

Nuclear forces are the strongest fundamental forces in nature, being approximately 100 times stronger than electromagnetic forces, making statement c true.

Nuclear forces are charge-independent, meaning the force between a proton-proton, neutron-neutron, or proton-neutron pair is essentially the same, making statement d true.

Since statement a claims that nuclear forces are central and independent of spin, it is the only false statement among the given options.

Answer: a

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A nucleus with mass number 190 initially at rest emits an alpha particle. If the $\mathrm{Q}$ value of the reaction is $4.5 \mathrm{~MeV}$, the kinetic energy of the alpha particle is
questions.solution:
Let $M$ be the mass of the parent nucleus, $m_{\alpha}$ be the mass of the alpha particle, and $m_d$ be the mass of the daughter nucleus. The mass number of the parent nucleus is $A = 190$. The alpha particle has a mass number of $4$, so the daughter nucleus has a mass number of $A - 4 = 186$.

From the conservation of linear momentum, since the parent nucleus is initially at rest, the magnitude of the momentum of the alpha particle must be equal to the magnitude of the momentum of the daughter nucleus: $p_{\alpha} = p_d$.

The kinetic energy $K$ is related to momentum $p$ by $K = \dfrac{p^2}{2m}$. Thus, the ratio of kinetic energies is $\dfrac{K_{\alpha}}{K_d} = \dfrac{p_{\alpha}^2 / 2m_{\alpha}}{p_d^2 / 2m_d} = \dfrac{m_d}{m_{\alpha}}$.

Using the mass numbers as an approximation for the masses, $m_{\alpha} \approx 4$ and $m_d \approx 186$. Therefore, $\dfrac{K_{\alpha}}{K_d} = \dfrac{186}{4} = 46.5$.

The total kinetic energy released is the Q-value: $K_{\alpha} + K_d = Q = 4.5 \text{ MeV}$.

Substituting $K_d = \dfrac{K_{\alpha}}{46.5}$ into the equation: $K_{\alpha} + \dfrac{K_{\alpha}}{46.5} = 4.5$.

$K_{\alpha} \left( 1 + \dfrac{1}{46.5} \right) = 4.5 \Rightarrow K_{\alpha} \left( \dfrac{47.5}{46.5} \right) = 4.5$.

$K_{\alpha} = 4.5 \times \dfrac{46.5}{47.5} \approx 4.405 \text{ MeV}$.

Answer: 4.4 MeV

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The radius of a nucleus as measured by electron scattering is $4.8 \mathrm{~fm}$. The mass number of nucleus is most likely to be
questions.solution:
The radius of a nucleus $R$ is related to its mass number $A$ by the formula $R = R_{0} A^{1/3}$, where $R_{0} \approx 1.2 \text{ fm}$.

Given $R = 4.8 \text{ fm}$, we have $4.8 = 1.2 \times A^{1/3}$.

Dividing both sides by $1.2$, we get $A^{1/3} = \dfrac{4.8}{1.2} = 4$.

Cubing both sides, $A = 4^{3} = 64$.

Answer: 64

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: $\text { If the nuclear radius of }{ }^{27} \mathrm{Al} \text { is } 3.6 \text { fermi, the nuclear radius of }{ }^{125} \mathrm{Fe} \text { is }$
questions.solution:
The nuclear radius $R$ is given by the formula $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$, where $R_0$ is a constant and $A$ is the mass number of the nucleus.

For $^{27}\mathrm{Al}$, the mass number $A_1 = 27$ and the radius $R_1 = 3.6 \text{ fermi}$.

Using the formula, $3.6 = R_0 (27)^{1/3} = R_0 \times 3$, which gives $R_0 = 1.2 \text{ fermi}$.

For $^{125}\mathrm{Fe}$, the mass number $A_2 = 125$. The radius $R_2$ is given by $R_2 = R_0 (125)^{1/3} = 1.2 \times 5 = 6.0 \text{ fermi}$.

Since $1 \text{ fermi} = 10^{-15} \text{ m}$, the radius $R_2 = 6.0 \times 10^{-15} \text{ m}$.

Answer: $6 \times 10^{-15} \mathrm{~m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The binding energy per nucleon for $\mathrm{C}^{12}$ is $7.68 \mathrm{~MeV}$ and that for $\mathrm{C}^{13}$ is $7.47 \mathrm{~MeV}$. The energy required to remove a neutron from $\mathrm{C}^{13}$ is
questions.solution:
The binding energy of a nucleus is given by $BE = A \times (BE/A)$, where $A$ is the mass number and $BE/A$ is the binding energy per nucleon.

For $\mathrm{C}^{12}$, $BE_{12} = 12 \times 7.68 \text{ MeV} = 92.16 \text{ MeV}$.

For $\mathrm{C}^{13}$, $BE_{13} = 13 \times 7.47 \text{ MeV} = 97.11 \text{ MeV}$.

The energy required to remove a neutron from $\mathrm{C}^{13}$ is the difference in binding energies: $\Delta E = BE_{13} - BE_{12} = 97.11 \text{ MeV} - 92.16 \text{ MeV} = 4.95 \text{ MeV}$.

Converting this energy to Joules using $1 \text{ MeV} = 1.6 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J}$:

$\Delta E = 4.95 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J} = 7.92 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J}$.

Answer: $7.92 \times 10^{-13} \mathrm{~J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The closest approach of an alpha particle when it make a head on collision with a gold nucleus is $10 \times 10^{-14} \mathrm{~m}$, then the kinetic energy of the alpha particle is :
questions.solution:
The distance of closest approach $r_0$ for an alpha particle of kinetic energy $K$ colliding head-on with a nucleus of atomic number $Z$ is given by the conservation of energy:

$K = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0} \dfrac{(Ze)(2e)}{r_0}$

For a gold nucleus, the atomic number $Z = 79$. The value of the Coulomb constant is $\dfrac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9 \text{ N m}^2 \text{ C}^{-2}$. The charge of an electron is $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.

Substituting the given values $r_0 = 10 \times 10^{-14} \text{ m} = 10^{-13} \text{ m}$:

$K = \dfrac{(9 \times 10^9) \times (79 \times 2) \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19})^2}{10^{-13}}$

$K = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times 158 \times 2.56 \times 10^{-38}}{10^{-13}}$

$K = 9 \times 158 \times 2.56 \times 10^{9 - 38 + 13}$

$K = 3640.32 \times 10^{-16} \text{ J}$

$K = 3.64032 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J}$

Rounding to the nearest value, we get $K = 3.64 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J}$.

Answer: $3.64 \times 10^{-13} \mathrm{~J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ratio of the radii of the nucleus of two element $\mathrm{X}$ and $\mathrm{Y}$ having the mass numbers 232 and 29 is:
questions.solution:
The radius of a nucleus is given by the formula $R = R_{0} A^{1/3}$, where $R_{0}$ is a constant and $A$ is the mass number of the nucleus.

For the two elements X and Y, the ratio of their radii is given by $\dfrac{R_{X}}{R_{Y}} = \dfrac{R_{0} A_{X}^{1/3}}{R_{0} A_{Y}^{1/3}} = \left( \dfrac{A_{X}}{A_{Y}} \right)^{1/3}$.

Given $A_{X} = 232$ and $A_{Y} = 29$, we substitute these values into the ratio:

$\dfrac{R_{X}}{R_{Y}} = \left( \dfrac{232}{29} \right)^{1/3}$.

Since $232 = 29 \times 8$, we have $\dfrac{232}{29} = 8$.

Therefore, $\dfrac{R_{X}}{R_{Y}} = (8)^{1/3} = 2$.

The ratio is $2 : 1$.

Answer: 2 : 1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Find the binding energy of the tritium nucleus:
[Given: mass of $1 \mathrm{H}^3=3.01605 \mathrm{~u} ; \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{p}}=1.00782 \mathrm{~u} ; \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{n}}=1.00866 \mathrm{~u}$.]
questions.solution:
The tritium nucleus $^{3}_{1}H$ consists of 1 proton and 2 neutrons.

Mass of constituents = $m_p + 2m_n = 1.00782 + 2 \times 1.00866 = 1.00782 + 2.01732 = 3.02514 \text{ u}$.

Mass defect $\Delta m = (m_p + 2m_n) - m_{nucleus} = 3.02514 - 3.01605 = 0.00909 \text{ u}$.

Binding energy = $\Delta m \times 931.5 \text{ MeV/u} = 0.00909 \times 931.5 \approx 8.467 \text{ MeV}$.

Rounding to the nearest given option, the binding energy is approximately 8.5 MeV.

Answer: 8.5 MeV

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The mass density of a nucleus varies with mass number $A$ as
questions.solution:
As, the mass density of a nucleus is constant
$\therefore \text { Mass density, }=\frac{3 m}{4 \pi R_0^3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following statement is true when a gamma decay occurs from the nucleus of an atom?
options: Mass number is reduced by 4 and atomic number is reduced by 2
Mass number is reduced by 4 and atomic number remains the same
Mass number remains the same and atomic number increases by 1
Mass number and atomic number are not changed
questions.solution:
Gamma decay involves the emission of high-energy electromagnetic radiation, known as gamma rays, from an excited nucleus to a lower energy state.

During this process, the nucleus does not lose any protons or neutrons. Consequently, the number of protons (atomic number, $Z$) and the total number of nucleons (mass number, $A$) remain unchanged.

The transition is represented as: _{Z}^{A}X^{*} \rightarrow _{Z}^{A}X + \gamma$.

Therefore, both the mass number and the atomic number remain constant.

Answer: Mass number and atomic number are not changed$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a nuclear reaction 2 deuteron nuclei combine to form a helium nucleus. The energy released in $\mathrm{MeV}$ will be: (Given mass of deuteron $=2.01355 \mathrm{~amu}$. and mass of helium nucleus $=4.0028 \mathrm{~amu}$.
questions.solution:
The nuclear reaction is given by: $2_{1}^{2}H \rightarrow _{2}^{4}He + Q$.

The mass of the reactants is $2 \times 2.01355 \text{ amu} = 4.02710 \text{ amu}$.

The mass of the product is $4.0028 \text{ amu}$.

The mass defect $\Delta m$ is calculated as: $\Delta m = (4.02710 - 4.0028) \text{ amu} = 0.0243 \text{ amu}$.

The energy released $Q$ is given by $Q = \Delta m \times 931.5 \text{ MeV/amu}$.

$Q = 0.0243 \times 931.5 \text{ MeV} \approx 22.62545 \text{ MeV}$.

Rounding to the nearest provided option, the energy released is $22.62 \text{ MeV}$.

Answer: 22.62 MeV

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The mass number of two nuclei $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$ are 27 and 125 respectively. The ratio of their radii $R_P: R_Q$ is given by:
questions.solution:
The radius $R$ of a nucleus with mass number $A$ is given by the relation $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$, where $R_0$ is a constant.

For nucleus $\mathrm{P}$, $A_P = 27$. Thus, $R_P = R_0 (27)^{1/3} = R_0 \times 3$.

For nucleus $\mathrm{Q}$, $A_Q = 125$. Thus, $R_Q = R_0 (125)^{1/3} = R_0 \times 5$.

The ratio of their radii is $\dfrac{R_P}{R_Q} = \dfrac{R_0 \times 3}{R_0 \times 5} = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

Therefore, the ratio $R_P : R_Q$ is $3 : 5$.

Answer: 3 : 5

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The mass density of a nucleus varies with mass number $A$ as
questions.solution:
The radius of a nucleus is given by the relation $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$, where $R_0$ is a constant and $A$ is the mass number.

The volume of the nucleus is $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi (R_0 A^{1/3})^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3 A$.

The mass of the nucleus is approximately $M = A \times m_p$, where $m_p$ is the mass of a nucleon.

The mass density $\rho$ is given by $\rho = \dfrac{M}{V} = \dfrac{A m_p}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3 A} = \dfrac{m_p}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3}$.

Since $m_p$, $R_0$, and $\pi$ are constants, the density $\rho$ is independent of the mass number $A$. Therefore, the density varies as $A^0$.

Answer: $\mathop A\limits^o $

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Ba-122 has half-life of $2 \mathrm{~min}$. Experiment has to be done using $B a-122$ and it takes 10 min to set up the experiment. It initially $80 \mathrm{~g}$ at $\mathrm{Ba}-122$ was taken, how much Ba was left when experiment was started?
questions.solution:
The half-life of Ba-122 is given as $T_{1/2} = 2 \text{ min}$.

The time elapsed before the experiment starts is $t = 10 \text{ min}$.

The number of half-lives $n$ that have passed is calculated as $n = \dfrac{t}{T_{1/2}} = \dfrac{10}{2} = 5$.

The amount of substance remaining $N$ after $n$ half-lives is given by the formula $N = N_0 \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^n$, where $N_0$ is the initial amount.

Given $N_0 = 80 \text{ g}$, we have $N = 80 \times \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^5$.

$N = 80 \times \dfrac{1}{32} = \dfrac{80}{32} = 2.5 \text{ g}$.

Answer: $2.5 \mathrm{~g}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When the speed of light becomes $\dfrac{2}{3}$ of its present value, the energy released in a given atomic explosion would:
options: decrease by $\dfrac{2}{3}$ of its initial value
decrease by $\dfrac{4}{9}$ of its initial value
decrease by $\dfrac{5}{9}$ of its initial value
decrease by $\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{9}$ of its initial value
questions.solution:
Initial energy: $E_i = \Delta mc^2$

New speed of light: $c' = \dfrac{2}{3}c$

New energy: $E_f = \Delta m \left(\dfrac{2}{3}c\right)^2 = \dfrac{4}{9}\Delta mc^2 = \dfrac{4}{9}E_i$

Decrease $= E_i - E_f = E_i - \dfrac{4}{9}E_i = \dfrac{5}{9}E_i$

The energy decreases by $\dfrac{5}{9}$ of its initial value.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following technique is not used for measuring small time intervals?
questions.solution:
Time measurement techniques are classified based on the physical phenomena involved. Electronic oscillators, such as quartz crystal oscillators, are used for precise timekeeping in electronic devices. Atomic clocks utilize the vibrations of atoms, such as cesium-133, to measure time with extreme precision. The decay of elementary particles is a fundamental process used in particle physics to measure extremely short time intervals. A spring oscillator, while periodic, is subject to significant damping, friction, and environmental factors, making it unsuitable for the precise measurement of small time intervals compared to the other high-precision methods listed.

Answer: Spring oscillator

questions.solution:

$N_{0}$ be the total amount of substance.
The amount of substance left after $N$ half-life is given by $\quad \frac{N}{N_{0}}=\frac{1}{2^{n}}$
Hence, $\quad \frac{30}{240}=\frac{1}{2^{n}}$
(Since, decay rate proportional to amount of substance)

\Rightarrow \quad 2^{n}=8 \Rightarrow n=3

Number of half-life passed $=3$
Time taken for the substance to decay from 240 count rate to 30 count rate $=1 \mathrm{~h}=60 \mathrm{~min}$
\begin{aligned}
\text { Half-life } &=\frac{\text { Total time }}{\text { Number of half - life }} \\
t_{1 / 2} &=\frac{60}{3}=20 \mathrm{~min}
\end{aligned}

Hence, remaining mass of the first substances after

\begin{aligned}

&=\frac{N_{0}}{2^{6}} \\

The number of half-lives in $50 \mathrm{~min}$,

n=\frac{t}{t_{1 / 2}}=\frac{50}{10}=5

In 5 half-lives, number of nuclei left undecayed,

N=N_{0}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n}=64 \times\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{5}=\frac{64}{32}=2

$\therefore$ Number of nuclei decayed $=N_{0}-N=64-2=62$
